messages:
sara: Hey team — drafting the post-incident comms for Kestrel (dedicated VPC / dedicated pool). They want an exec-friendly summary + technical RCA + proposed credits by EOD tomorrow. I sketched a short exec summary below, would love: (1) cause blurb, (2) impact window + % of traffic, (3) mitigation steps taken, (4) suggested credits. Pls drop quick bullets and any wording edits.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1809123456 | sev2 | triggered 2025-11-02T15:34:16Z | affected: kestrel-prod (dedicated pool #kestrel-01) | symptom: increased 5xx and tail latency | status: mitigated 2025-11-02T16:22:49Z | pager: @mike_oncall, @jess_engsre

mike_oncall: short tech summary: we hit transient KV-cache eviction storms after a model swap during a rolling deploy. cache miss rate shot from ~3% to 47% for ~20m which caused synchronous fetches to upstream s3-backed shard to queue; tail latency + error budget burn. I have traces and top spans if needed.

jess_engsre: adding details from traces: spike correlates to a deployment that changed seq-length config -> larger KV entries -> evictions. also saw two worker nodes repeatedly OOM+restart because we had slightly lower memory headroom after config change.

oliver_prod: impact numbers from console: affected requests = 12.4% of kestrel-prod QPS during window; error rate peaked 6.8% (baseline 0.02%). latency p95 moved from 220ms -> 1.8s. Customer reported 3 degraded requests to their SRE team.

caroline_acct: Kestrel leadership is sensitive. They're on a tight release cycle and asked for an exec call if we propose credits. They asked for a short timeline to present to their COO — they want no more than a 1-slide summary.

sara: proposed exec summary draft (very short):

```
On 2025-11-02 a configuration change during a model rollout to Kestrel's dedicated pool caused an unexpected increase in KV cache entry size, triggering widespread cache evictions and a downstream spike in upstream fetch latency. The issue was mitigated within ~48 minutes by: halting the rollout, reverting the config, and applying temporary per-tenant cache soft-limits while we validated a safer quantization profile. Impact: ~12% of requests experienced elevated latency and a peak error-rate of 6.8%. Next steps: permanent fix is a config validation check plus a guardrail in the deployment pipeline; proposed credit: one week of reserved capacity credit (or equivalent usage credit).
```

mike_oncall: suggested technical wording edit: swap `quantization profile` -> `model chunking/seq-length config` — quantization wasn't changed. Also add: "we applied a temporary model-variant downgrade for Kestrel while we backfilled the cache".

jess_engsre: RCA bullets for the full article (detailed):
- Timeline: 15:34 deploy start -> 15:37 first elevated 5xx -> 15:56 mitigation (pause+revert) -> 16:22 full recovery
- Root cause: regression in deployment config that increased per-token cache footprint without validating memory headroom for dedicated pool sizes
- Contrib factors: lack of per-pool sanity check, aggressive rollout schedule, missing OOM alert threshold tuning for worker nodes
- Mitigation applied: halted rollout, reverted config, applied per-tenant cache soft-limits and temporary model downgrade, restarted affected workers with adjusted memory flags
- Long-term fixes: pre-deploy validation, spike-protected KV eviction algorithm, alert: per-node memory reclaim 3x before restart, staging rollout that simulates increased seq-length workloads

caroline_acct: on credits — they asked for a number. Oliver, can you propose one we can justify? prefer usage-based credit vs flat reserved-week. Kestrel's finance team prefers a percent-of-bill approach.

oliver_prod: rough calc: impacted window ~48m during business hours. Their avg daily spend on dedicated pool ~$12k/day. If we do pro-rata for the window and give a 3x goodwill multiplier => ~ (12k * (48/1440)) * 3 = ~$1,200. Alternative: one week reserved capacity credit = ~$7k — feels high. Recommend we offer the percent approach: 10% of that day's bill => ~$1200. Propose we offer $1,200 credit and a free 2-week increased burst capacity for frictionless rollouts.

sara: customer-facing language for credits: "We’d like to offer a $1,200 usage credit to account for the degraded window, plus two weeks of complimentary burst capacity to support your upcoming releases." Thoughts? @tara_legal need sign-off on wording re: "free" capacity?

tara_legal: quick note: avoid language implying admission of negligence. Use: "as a gesture of goodwill" instead of "to account for". Also clear that credits applied per our TOS and don't change SLA language. ok to offer burst capacity short-term, legal has no issue with that wording.

jess_engsre: small technical addendum for the comms: include a bullet that says "no customer data was exposed" — important for their compliance team. Verified.

caroline_acct: scheduling: Kestrel asked for a 30m exec call tomorrow at 09:00 PT. Can someone from eng to join for 15m? @mike_oncall and @jess_engsre are you available?

mike_oncall: I can join at 09:00 PT.

jess_engsre: I can do 09:00 PT but may need to jump in for the first 20m.

sara: ok — plan: I will send the 1-slide exec summary + proposed credit wording (legal-approved) and an attachment with the detailed RCA. Action items: 
- @jess_engsre finalize detailed RCA doc and tech appendix (today EOD)
- @mike_oncall provide traces and span samples to attach (today EOD)
- @oliver_prod finalize credit calc and billing code to redeem (today EOD)
- @caroline_acct coordinate call time and attendee list, send calendar invite
- @tara_legal approve final customer message wording (ASAP)

sara: final ask — please paste any redlines here. If we agree by 18:00 PT I'll send the customer package and calendar invite. Thanks all :thumbsup:
